overview.description: Top Trumps is a comparison card game in which each player holds themed cards showing one item (e.g. a car, a dinosaur) and several numerical attributes. The starting player names an attribute; everyone reveals that attribute's value from their top card; the highest (or best) value wins the round and the winner takes all those cards. The winner then chooses the next attribute. Play continues until one player has won all the cards. The game was first published in the UK in 1978 and is popular with families and children.
overview.deck: Themed pack (typically 30, 32, 48 or 50 cards per deck)

history.origins: Country/Region of Origin: United Kingdom. Time Period: 1978. Historical Development: Top Trumps was first published by Dubreq in 1978 with eleven themed packs; Dubreq was taken over by Waddingtons in 1982, who continued until the early 1990s. Winning Moves UK acquired the rights in 1992 and relaunched the game with many new themes. Cultural Significance: Popular playground and family game, especially with children; themed packs cover vehicles, military hardware, sports, films, and wildlife.

setup.dealing: All cards are dealt as equally as possible to the players. Each player holds their cards in a face-down stack so that only their top card is visible to them; opponents cannot see a player's cards. The starting player is normally the player to the dealer's left.

rules.objective: Win all the cards by repeatedly winning rounds: in each round the active player chooses an attribute, everyone reveals that attribute's value from their top card, and the player with the highest (or best) value takes all the cards played that round and chooses the next attribute. The game ends when one player has collected the entire pack.
rules.gameplay: 1. Setup: Deal all cards as equally as possible; each player holds their cards in a face-down stack, viewing only the top card. 2. Play: The starting player (normally left of dealer) chooses one attribute and reads its value from their top card; each other player reads the same attribute from their top card. The best value (usually highest; for some attributes like weight or time, lowest is better) wins the round. 3. Winner takes all the top cards from that round and places them at the bottom of their stack, then chooses the next attribute from their new top card. 4. Ties: If two or more players tie for best value, all played cards go to the center; the same player chooses again from the next card; the winner of that round also takes the center pile. If a player has no data for the chosen attribute, treat as a tie. 5. Elimination: Players drop out when they have no cards left. The winner is the player who collects the whole pack.
keyRules: Only the top card of each player's stack is in play each round
The player who won the previous round chooses the attribute for the next round
Best value wins the round (usually highest; some attributes use lowest-is-best)
On a tie or no-data, cards go to the center; same player chooses again; next round winner takes center pile too

strategy.basic: Choose attributes where your top card's value is strong relative to what you have seen. Avoid categories where your card is weak.
strategy.intermediate: Remember which attribute values have already been played or are likely on opponents' cards. When you are likely to lose a round, sometimes choosing an attribute where you might tie forces a center pile and gives you another chance to choose.
strategy.advanced: Track the distribution of values across the pack if possible; prioritise winning when you can choose so you keep the lead and control the category.
tips: Pick categories where your visible card ranks highly
On a weak card, consider choosing an attribute that might tie to get another turn
Winning the round lets you choose the next attribute from your new top card

difficulty.easy: Choose a random legal attribute when it is the AI's turn to choose; compare values and award the round to the highest (or best) value.
difficulty.medium: Prefer attributes where the AI's top card has a strong value; simple tracking of which attributes have been played.
difficulty.hard: Model likely attribute values on opponents' cards; choose attributes to maximise win probability and avoid categories where the AI's card is weak.

considerations: AI must only choose from attributes present on the current top card.
On ties or no-data, the same player chooses again; AI must handle center pile correctly.
Theme packs vary (cars, dinosaurs, etc.); attribute names and highest-vs-lowest semantics are pack-dependent.

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck comprising four suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades. Each suit contains thirteen ranks: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King, providing versatile options for various card games.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card iconography and distinct color coding for easy identification.
engine.rankDescription: Standard thirteen ranks per suit: Ace, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, and King, where each rank has distinct value and meaning depending on the specific game rules and player strategies.
